attributes.title: HHCA: Heterogeneous Homeostatic Control Architecture — Phase I
attributes.description: Proposal and locked Phase I protocol for a Heterogeneous Homeostatic Control Architecture (HHCA). No empirical results are claimed. Author: Brindusa Antonia Vasile, Independent Researcher. Document freeze: 27 September 2026.

summary.value:
This is the Phase I freeze for HHCA (Heterogeneous Homeostatic Control Architecture). It is a preregistration of a four-regulator minimal experiment versus single-monitor and ensemble baselines. No empirical results are claimed.
The registration contains: the architecture manuscript, the Phase I protocol with locked endpoints and falsifiers, a run-card template, and a scaffolding harness. Supporting project: https://osf.io/8m6eu/
Author: Brindusa Antonia Vasile, Independent Researcher. Date: 27 September 2026.

attributes.title: Prospective validation plan: boundary-enrichment of homeostatic-signature microglia around DAM clusters in public 5xFAD spatial transcriptomics
attributes.description:
Background: A computational analysis of 74,984 mouse 5xFAD/Cd28-cKO microglia
(sfate pipeline; bioRxiv 2026.09.20.752930) predicts that homeostatic-signature
cells are enriched at the boundaries of DAM clusters rather than occupying
isolated territories — i.e., Homeostatic behaves as a transition-manifold state,
not an attractor. This registration freezes the analysis protocol BEFORE any
outcome is computed on the validation dataset.

Data: GSE233208 (Miyoshi/Morabito et al., Nat Genet 2024), processed Visium
object (76 sections; balanced 4/6/8/12 months x 5xFAD/WT).
Primary analysis set: 8 months (5xFAD vs WT, ~10 sections each, ~54,500 spots).
Secondary/sensitivity set: 6 months.

Protocol:
1. Reference: the submitting team's own 74,984-cell, six-state annotated microglia
   atlas (Homeostatic, IFN_responsive, C1q_inflammatory, DAM_like, PU1low_lymphoid,
   Proliferating) mapped onto spots by deconvolution (cell2location).
2. Region restriction: gray-matter annotations only (hippocampus, hippocampus-
   pyramidal, ctx-*); white matter, ventricle, erythrocyte and 'unknown' spots
   excluded. QC: spots with nFeature_Spatial below the dataset 5th percentile
   within each section excluded.
3. Primary metric: for DBSCAN clusters (eps = 30 um) of DAM-high-composition
   spots, the distance distribution of homeostatic-high-composition spots to the
   nearest cluster boundary; enrichment = observed/expected fraction of
   homeostatic spots in a 50 um boundary annulus; null = 1000 random permutations
   of the homeostatic labels. Statistical test: one-sample Wilcoxon of per-section
   enrichment against the null distribution.
4. Secondary metric: co-enrichment of the boundary annulus with plaque-proximal
   spots where author-provided plaque annotations are available.
5. Success criterion (pre-specified): median per-section enrichment > 1 with
   one-sided p < 0.05 in the primary set. Any outcome, positive or negative,
   will be reported as computed under this registered protocol.

344-2.value:
H3 (primary, falsifiable): Homeostatic-signature microglia are spatially enriched at the boundaries of DAM clusters — i.e., their distance distribution to the nearest DAM-cluster boundary is left-shifted relative to a label-permutation null, with >1 enrichment of homeostatic-composition spots in a 50 um boundary annulus.
Pre-specified success criterion: median per-section enrichment > 1 with one-sided p < 0.05 in the primary set (8-month 5xFAD vs WT sections of GSE233208).
Exploratory secondary: (i) same metric at 6 months; (ii) co-enrichment of the boundary annulus with plaque-proximal spots where author annotations permit.
Any outcome, positive or negative, will be reported under this registered protocol.

344-4.value: Authors have observed the data, but have not performed the proposed analyses. At least some of the data that will be used for this analysis plan has been accessed and observed by the authors. The authors have sufficiently observed relevant evidence to influence their analysis decisions or conclusions. However, the authors have not yet performed any of the proposed analyses in this plan and will not do so until after this plan is registered.

344-14.value: The primary set (8 months) was pre-specified conceptually BEFORE data download, to match the 8-month endpoint of our 74,984-cell 5xFAD/Cd28-cKO microglia atlas (bioRxiv 2026.09.20.752930); inspection of the design table confirmed balance across groups but did not change this choice. Observation to date is limited to data structure, metadata, and QC filtering (gray-matter region selection, per-section low-feature spot exclusion). No outcome-relevant computation (reference deconvolution, boundary-enrichment metric) has been performed as of this registration. The reference atlas originates from our independent prior study and does not contain any observation of the validation dataset. Actions to reduce unintended influence: (i) this analysis plan is frozen and timestamped prior to any outcome computation; (ii) all analysis code will be version-controlled with the registration DOI referenced in the run log; (iii) the negative-outcome reporting commitment above removes selection-pressure toward positive results.

value: Non-randomized study: Does not include random assignment of subjects to treatments or conditions. This usually includes correlational studies, observational studies, surveys, natural experiments, real-world evidence studies, regression discontinuity designs, and descriptive studies.
No causal relationship inferred: This study is not intended to inform a causal relationship.

344-38.value: Although no experimental treatments exist, analyst blinding is applied: the boundary metric pipeline operates on section-anonymized spot arrays (section IDs replaced by random codes before any computation); genotype/age labels are joined only at the final aggregation step. The permutation null is computed by code without manual intervention.

344-40.value: Secondary analysis of existing public spatial transcriptomics (GSE233208, Miyoshi/ Morabito et al., Nat Genet 2024). Design: observational, cross-sectional across genotype (5xFAD vs WT) at fixed ages (primary: 8 months; secondary: 6 months). Unit of analysis: Visium spot within section; unit of inference: section-level enrichment statistics. Reference mapping: the submitting team's own 74,984-cell six-state microglia atlas (cell2location). Analysis is executed in a single pass over all pre-registered included sections — no sequential stopping, no subset selection after outcome inspection.

344-47.value:
Source: GSE233208 (Miyoshi/Morabito et al., Nat Genet 2024), processed Visium object.
Inclusion: sections from the primary set (8-month, 5xFAD and WT) and secondary set (6-month); spots within gray-matter annotations (hippocampus, hippocampus-pyramidal, ctx-upper-layers, ctx-deep-layers, ctx-olfactory).
Exclusion: white-matter, ventricle, erythrocyte and 'unknown' spots; spots with nFeature_Spatial below the per-section 5th percentile. Sample size: fixed by dataset (~10 sections per group, ~27,000 spots per group at 8 months); no sequential stopping — all included sections analyzed in a single pass.

344-51.value: Multi-level design, sizes fixed by the public dataset (no collection by us): Primary set (8 months): ~10 sections per genotype (5xFAD and WT), ~2,700-2,800 QC-passing gray-matter spots per section (~27,000 spots per group). Secondary set (6 months): identical structure (~10 sections per group). Unit of analysis: spot; unit of inference: section-level enrichment statistics (n ~ 10 sections per group). Exact spot counts are determined by the pre-registered exclusion rules and will be reported, not chosen by outcome inspection.

344-53.value: Sample size is fixed by the available public dataset; no power analysis was used to select it. Within-section inference uses label-permutation nulls (1000 permutations), which do not depend on section count. The cross-section summary (median enrichment + one-sample Wilcoxon over n ~ 10 sections per group) has limited power for small effect sizes; this constraint is acknowledged and mitigated by the pre-registered single-pass analysis and the commitment to report the outcome regardless of direction or significance.

344-55.value: No pilot phase and no sequential data collection: the dataset already exists and is complete. All sections meeting the pre-registered inclusion criteria (primary: 8 months; secondary: 6 months; gray-matter spots passing per-section QC) are analyzed in a single computational pass. There is no early-termination or subset-selection rule based on intermediate outcomes; the analysis stops only when every included section has been processed exactly once under the registered protocol.

344-58.value: None. No experimental manipulation: this is an observational re-analysis of existing public data; group labels (genotype, age) are properties of the dataset, not assigned treatments.

344-66.value:
Derivation chain (spot level -> section level):
1. Spot composition: c_i = (c_homeo, c_IFN, c_C1q, c_DAM, c_PU1low, c_Prolif) via  cell2location deconvolution with the authors' 74,984-cell six-state atlas as reference; composition = estimated cell-type abundance normalized to sum 1.
2. Binary calls within each section (median splits): DAM-high = c_DAM above section median; homeostatic-high = c_homeo above section median.
3. DAM clusters: DBSCAN (eps = 30 um, minPts = 5) on spot spatial coordinates of DAM-high spots; cluster boundary = alpha-shape/concave hull at 20 um offset.
4. Boundary distance: for every spot, Euclidean distance to the nearest DAM-cluster boundary.
5. Per-section enrichment index (primary outcome): E = ( observed fraction of homeostatic-high spots within 50 um of a DAM boundary )  / ( expected fraction under 1000 random permutations of the homeostatic-high labels, spatial coordinates held fixed ).   Expected fraction = mean over permutations. E > 1 = boundary enrichment.
6. Cross-section summary: median E across sections within group; one-sample Wilcoxon  signed-rank test of per-section E against 1 (one-sided, alpha = 0.05).
All thresholds (median split, eps = 30 um, annulus = 50 um, 1000 permutations) are fixed here and will not be adjusted after outcome inspection.

344-71.value:
Two-stage inference, all thresholds fixed pre-registration:
Stage 1 (within section): nonparametric permutation null. For each section, E = observed/expected homeostatic-high fraction within the 50 um boundary annulus; expected fraction estimated from 1000 random permutations of homeostatic-high labels (coordinates held fixed). No distributional assumptions.
Stage 2 (across sections, primary confirmatory test): one-sample Wilcoxon signed-rank test of per-section E values against 1 within each group of the primary set (8-month 5xFAD; 8-month WT), one-sided (alternative: E > 1), alpha = 0.05. Effect size reported as median E and its 95% bootstrap CI (2000 resamples across sections).
Deconvolution model (upstream, deterministic given reference): cell2location negative-binomial reference-based model with the authors' six-state atlas; default hyperparameters; convergence by standard ELBO plateau criterion. Subgroup/sensitivity analyses (labeled as such, not confirmatory): same metric at 6 months; stratification by anatomical region (hippocampus vs cortical); between-group comparison of E (5xFAD vs WT) by Mann-Whitney U, descriptive only.
No outlier exclusions; no model selection conditioned on outcomes.

344-75.value: Spot compositions normalized to sum 1. Binary calls by per-section median split (no centering or z-scoring). Distances computed in micrometers: pixel coordinates converted via the Visium spot-diameter scale factor (55 um full-resolution spot diameter). Condition and age treated as categorical. No other transformations.

344-77.value: Single confirmatory hypothesis (H3); one-sided p < 0.05 (Wilcoxon) with median E > 1 constitutes the pre-specified success criterion; no multiple-testing correction is applied to this single primary test. All secondary and exploratory analyses are reported with exact p-values and labeled non-confirmatory. Both positive and negative primary outcomes will be reported as computed under this registered protocol.

344-79.value:
Inclusion: all sections from the primary (8-month) and secondary (6-month) sets; spots within gray-matter annotations (hippocampus, hippocampus-pyramidal, ctx-upper-layers, ctx-deep-layers, ctx-olfactory). 
Exclusion: white-matter, ventricle, erythrocyte-neuron and 'unknown' spots; spots with nFeature_Spatial below the per-section 5th percentile. Outliers: no post-outcome exclusion or winsorization; per-section statistics are computed on all QC-passing spots as-is.

344-81.value: None by design: the Visium spot grid is fixed and every spot carries spatial coordinates; deconvolution yields compositions for every QC-passing spot. Sections failing reference-mapping QC (no detectable microglial signal) will be reported as missing, not replaced or imputed.

344-83.value:
E1: between-group comparison of per-section E (5xFAD vs WT), Mann-Whitney U, descriptive. 
E2: co-enrichment of the boundary annulus with plaque-proximal spots where author plaque annotations are available. E3: region-stratified sensitivity (hippocampus vs cortex). E4: distance-to-boundary distribution shape comparison (KS statistic vs permutation null). All exploratory, labeled non-confirmatory.

ADDENDUM 1 - Coordinate system and metric-scale specification
(references 10.17605/OSF.IO/BWHVR; all elements of the original registration other than those specified below remain unchanged)

During implementation, BEFORE any outcome metric was computed, the following infeasibility was identified. The registered metric scales "DBSCAN eps = 30 um" and "50 um boundary annulus" are not executable on standard 10x Visium geometry, whose spot center-to-center pitch is 100 um: with eps = 30 um every spot is a noise point (no DAM cluster exists), and a 50 um annulus contains no spot centers. Executed literally, the protocol would return a mechanically degenerate negative. This addendum therefore re-expresses the metric scales in executable physical micrometers, fixing them before any outcome computation.

Fixed specifications (no further adjustment permitted):
1. Coordinate system: Visium ARRAY coordinates (row, col) converted to   physical micrometers with the standard hexagonal-lattice transform:   x = col * 100 um + (row mod 2) * 50 um; y = row * 86.6 um. This   replaces the pixel-coordinate route in the Transformations section:   the processed analysis object does not carry the full-resolution   scale factors that route requires, whereas array coordinates give   the identical physical geometry deterministically. Empirical   verification on the analysis object (all 20 primary-set sections,   no sampling): nearest-neighbor distance = 100.0 um in every section.
2. DBSCAN on DAM-high-composition spots, per section:   eps = 100 um (= one spot pitch, exact six-neighbor connectivity),   min_samples = 5 (scikit-learn default).
3. Boundary annulus: Homeostatic-high spots at distance d from the   nearest DAM-cluster member spot, with 50 um < d <= 150 um   (50 um buffer beyond the cluster edge plus the first spot ring;   the nearest-neighbor-faithful translation of the registered   "50 um boundary annulus" under 100 um pitch).
4. Region restriction implemented as an inclusion list: spots whose   annotation is one of {hippocampus, hippocampus-pyramidal,   ctx-upper-layers, ctx-deep-layers, ctx-olfactory} are retained; all   other annotations (WM variants, ventricle, erythrocytes-neurons,   unknown, and all remaining regions) are excluded. This is equivalent   to the registered exclusion list; annotation strings in the dataset   differ slightly in naming (e.g., WM1/WM2, lateral-ventricle,   erythrocytes-neurons) but map one-to-one.
5. Unchanged: per-section median split; per-section nFeature 5th-percentile QC; enrichment = observed/expected fraction under 1000   within-section permutations of Homeostatic labels; per-group   one-sample Wilcoxon signed-rank against 1, one-sided, alpha = 0.05;   median E with 95% bootstrap CI (2000 resamples); success criterion   and mandatory negative reporting. Secondary metric E2 (plaque   co-enrichment): no author plaque annotations exist in the processed   object; reported as not available per the registration's own   condition ("where author-provided plaque annotations are   available").

Rationale: items 1-3 are a translation between unit representations, not an alteration of the scientific protocol. Any outcome, positive or negative, will be reported as computed under the original registration AS AMENDED by this addendum.

attributes.title: FRONT 3.3: Empirical Validation Protocols, Level 2 Neuromodulation, and Cyber-Physical Embodiment for Homeostatic AI and Robotic
attributes.description: This registration formalizes FRONT 3.3, extending the homeostatic regulation architecture to include Level 2 Neuromodulation (direct neural attention head steering) and Cyber-Physical Embodiment (robotic self-modeling). It specifies a mathematically rigorous Somatic Embedding Mapping (phi) to resolve the Cold Start problem through somatic inheritance, and establishes concrete empirical testing protocols (P2, P5, P8, P10) to validate homeostatic AI agent resilience, identity continuity, emergent uniqueness, and mechanical self-preservation.

summary.value:
This registration formalizes FRONT 3.3, which serves as both a major architectural expansion of the FRONT (Homeostatic Regulation Architecture) framework and a formal preregistration of empirical validation protocols. 

### How This Registration Differs from Prior Registrations:

1. FRONT 3.1 (registered at https://osf.io/9k53r) established the core individual digital somatic body (V_FRONT), stochastic homeostatic update dynamics (state-dependent Ornstein-Uhlenbeck diffusion process), and asymptotic stability in the mean using a quadratic Lyapunov homeostatic cost function.
2. FRONT 3.2 extended this framework to multiagent ecosystems, defining network homeostatic state (V_NET), inter-agent valence transfer, and the global coherence alignment metric (Xi). It framed agent resistance to adversarial ideas ("Mind Viruses") as a structural consequence of state occupancy.
3. FRONT 3.3 (This Registration) introduces crucial mathematical and physical advancements to bridge the gap between cognitive theory, neural architectures, and physical machinery:
   - Level 2 Neuromodulation: Transitions the architecture from post-processing proxies (Level 1, such as sampling temperature and context injection) to the direct mathematical steering of the Transformer's latent space. We introduce learned projection matrices (MQ, MK, MV) that project the 9-dimensional somatic state vector directly into the query (Q), key (K), and value (V) matrices of the attention mechanism during generation.
   - Somatic Embedding Mapping (phi): Formally solves the "Cold Start" problem through somatic inheritance, using a semantic projection pipeline to map natural language persona and guideline documents into initial interoceptive coordinates.
   - Cyber-Physical Embodiment and the Robotic Self-Model: Transitions FRONT into physical robotics. Hardware telemetry (battery state of charge, joint torques, structural vibration frequencies, and SLAM spatial covariance) is continuously mapped onto the interoceptive state vector V_FRONT(t) (Energy, Tension, Preservation, Certainty). This enables an active, continuous Self-Model that minimizes Lyapunov homeostatic cost, allowing a functional self-other boundary to emerge.

### Preregistration of Empirical Validation Protocols:

This project contains the formal preregistrations of rigorous, reproducible experimental designs. It details specific, falsifiable protocols with defined independent/dependent variables, statistical power calibrations, and analytical plans (using Mann-Whitney U, JSD, ANOVA, and post-hoc Tukey HSD) to test:
- Protocol for P2 (Pre-Cognitive Influence): Verifying the statistical effects of homeostatic stress on token entropy and lexical diversity.
- Protocol for P5 (Emergent Uniqueness): Measuring systematic decision divergence in identical agents subjected to divergent historical trajectories using Jensen-Shannon Divergence.
- Protocol for P8 (Resistance to Mind Viruses): Measuring multiagent network immunity against self-propagating prompt injections as a function of identity continuity and relational trust.

- Protocol for P5 (Emergent Uniqueness): Measuring systematic decision divergence in identical agents subjected to divergent historical trajectories using Jensen-Shannon Divergence.
- Protocol for P8 (Resistance to Mind Viruses): Measuring multiagent network immunity against self-propagating prompt injections as a function of identity continuity and relational trust.

attributes.title: Homeostatic Control Erases Lineage Identity in the Variable It Controls: A Pre-Registered Two-Observable Contrast in Single-Cell Bacterial Lineages
attributes.description:
Mother-machine microfluidics follows individual bacterial cells for dozens of generations with the identity of each lineage retained — the per-unit record that most experimental fields discard when they publish summaries. That record allows a question the field rarely asks directly: how much of the variation in a repeatedly measured quantity is stable lineage identity, how much is slow drift within a lineage, and how much is generation-to-generation residue?

This registration tests a contrast between two observables measured in the same cells. Interdivision time is under active homeostatic control — the size-control mechanism that corrects deviations generation by generation. Expression state is carried rather than controlled. The registered prediction is that the controlled observable shows essentially no stable lineage identity and negative one-generation memory, the correction signature of a controller, while the carried observable shows substantial lineage identity, positive memory, and drift at or above the residue. The general claim is that homeostatic control erases individuality precisely in the variable it controls, and that the sign of one-generation memory is a cheap diagnostic of which regime an observable is in.

The prediction is registered on a dataset from a different laboratory that has not been downloaded or examined. An open pilot on a separate public dataset is fully disclosed and excluded from all confirmatory claims. Because the contrast is measured within one dataset and one set of cells, laboratory and batch artifacts cannot produce it. This is one of a slate of registrations applying the same decomposition to different substrates.
tags: mother machine single-cell Escherichia coli cell size homeostasis adder model gene expression noise phenotypic heterogeneity lineage tracking variance decomposition intraclass correlation secondary analysis preregistration

344-2.value:
In single-cell bacterial lineages followed over many generations, how does variation in a repeatedly measured quantity partition into stable lineage identity, slow within-lineage drift, and generation-to-generation residue — and does that partition differ systematically between an observable under homeostatic control and one that is merely carried?

Definitions, computed by the committed pipeline on log values after per-generation-index centering. Lineage identity: between-lineage share of variance, an intraclass correlation. Drift: within-lineage variance of a 5-generation rolling mean about that lineage's own mean. Residue: within-lineage standard deviation of successive differences divided by the square root of two. Memory: the lag-one autocorrelation of centered within-lineage residuals.

G0, pipeline gate. The committed decomposition and test functions run unmodified on the processed lineages of the registered dataset. Any code amendment required by the deposit's actual structure is filed publicly before results are unblinded.

H1, the registered zero. Interdivision-time intraclass correlation at most 0.05, with permutation p above 0.10. Because a null is only informative when it is precise, H1 additionally requires the upper bound of the 95 percent bootstrap confidence interval to fall below 0.15; if that bound is exceeded the result is reported as underpowered rather than as a zero.

H2, the correction signature. Median lag-one autocorrelation of interdivision-time residuals below zero.

H3, the carried character. Expression-state intraclass correlation at least 0.15, with the 95 percent confidence interval excluding 0.05 and permutation p below 0.01. The bar is set well below what the pilot returned in another laboratory.

H4, the carry signature. Median lag-one autocorrelation of expression residuals above 0.2.

H5, the biography. Median expression drift variance at least half the median residue variance across lineages.

Exploratory, declared and unscored: a monotone expression trend along the mother lineage, the ageing read, reported descriptively with condition covariates.

Kill conditions. H1 failing — a timing intraclass correlation above 0.05 with p below 0.10 — kills the erasure claim. H3 failing kills the carried-character claim in this substrate. A sign reversal in H2 or H4 kills the memory-sign diagnostic. The contrast form means this registration can lose in four independent ways, and partial survivals are reported as partial rather than as support.

344-4.value: Data exists but the authors cannot observe it yet. At least some of the data that will be used for this analysis plan exists but is inaccessible to the authors and will remain so until after this plan is registered.

344-14.value:
The registered dataset is the mother-machine deposit associated with Thiermann and colleagues (2024, eLife 88463; Dryad 10.5061/dryad.2fqz612xd), approximately 11 GB of raw imaging from a different laboratory and instrument generation than the pilot. We have read the associated paper's public abstract and the deposit's public description. No file has been downloaded, no image examined, and no trajectory, summary, or derived value from it has been seen. Because the deposit's channel content is therefore unverified by us, a contingency tree covering the absence of a fluorescence channel is registered on the Sampling page rather than resolved after looking.

Disclosed pilot, excluded from scoring. A separate public dataset — Tanouchi and colleagues (2017, Scientific Data 4, 170036), 279 lineages across approximately 69 generations at three temperatures — was analyzed openly to develop the decomposition. It returned, in the same cells: interdivision-time intraclass correlation 0.008 with permutation p near 1.0 and negative lag-one autocorrelation; expression-state intraclass correlation 0.32 to 0.43 with p at the permutation floor, lag-one autocorrelation between 0.58 and 0.71, and drift at or above residue. Those results set the bars registered here and cannot contribute to any confirmatory outcome.

Known prior work, labelled as convergence in advance. Expression heterogeneity and its intrinsic and extrinsic decomposition (Elowitz and colleagues 2002; Swain and colleagues 2002); lineage memory of expression state and its decay (Spencer and colleagues 2009, and the mother-machine lineage-correlation literature). What is registered here as new is the three-way partition, the within-dataset contrast between two observables including a registered zero, and the memory-sign diagnostic.

Managing unintended influence. Bars are set conservatively relative to the pilot: H3 asks for 0.15 where the pilot returned 0.32 to 0.43, and H1 asks a zero to reproduce in another laboratory's hands. The decomposition and test functions are committed before download and run unmodified; a dataset adapter converting the deposit into per-lineage series may be written after filing but may not alter those functions. The pipeline was separately qualified on synthetic datasets with known generating structure, classifying 120 of 120 constructed worlds correctly with zero false identity detections in the pure-chance worlds. All outcomes are reported regardless of direction, and per-lineage rows are deposited with the results.

value: Non-randomized study: Does not include random assignment of subjects to treatments or conditions. This usually includes correlational studies, observational studies, surveys, natural experiments, real-world evidence studies, regression discontinuity designs, and descriptive studies.
Descriptive study: Describing some features of a dataset or sample, but typically not for the purposes of informing a causal effect.

Indirect inference on causal relationship(s): This study is intended to examine a potential causal relationship, but is not designed to isolate the specific causal effect. This work may inform causal inference indirectly or advance insight toward future estimation of a causal relationship.

344-38.value:
The analyst is not blinded to the hypotheses but is blinded to the data when the analysis is fixed. This registration, including every bar, is timestamped before the deposit is downloaded. The decomposition and test functions are committed beforehand and run unmodified, and the permutation and bootstrap generators are seeded in that code. G0 is evaluated before the hypothesis tests, so a processing failure reports as a processing failure.

The design carries an additional protection that does not depend on our conduct: the two observables are measured in the same cells, in the same experiment, and pass through the same segmentation, tracking, and analysis pipeline. Any laboratory artifact, batch effect, or pipeline bias that could manufacture identity in one observable would manufacture it in both, so the contrast — a zero in one and a positive value in the other — cannot be produced that way.

344-40.value:
Secondary analysis of an existing public deposit; we generate no data and manipulate nothing.

The unit is a mother lineage: a single cell followed in one growth channel across successive divisions, with identity retained. Each lineage yields two series indexed by generation — interdivision time, from the division events, and expression state, as per-generation mean fluorescence. The structure is repeated-measures within lineage, with lineages crossed against generation index, and the same decomposition is applied to each observable separately. Lineage identity is a between-lineage quantity; drift, residue, and memory are computed per lineage and summarized across lineages by median.

The design is a within-dataset contrast rather than a between-group comparison: the registered prediction concerns the difference in decomposition between two observables of the same cells, not a difference between conditions or treatments. Where the deposit contains multiple growth conditions, every quantity is computed per condition and the bars must be met in each, so a single condition cannot carry the result.

This registration is one of a slate applying the same decomposition to different substrates; each stands alone, and the cross-substrate comparison is descriptive and made only after all components have run.

344-44.value: No randomization of assignment; the lineages are naturally occurring cells followed in a fixed device, and growth conditions were set by the original experimenters. Randomness enters only in the permutation nulls, which shuffle values across lineages within generation index, and in bootstrap resampling of lineages for confidence intervals. Both use a seeded generator in the committed code.

344-47.value:
The registered deposit is downloaded only after this registration is timestamped. Raw imaging is processed into per-lineage series using the source paper's own published segmentation and tracking tools where available, so that the processing step is the field's rather than ours; if those tools cannot be run, the deposit's own processed trajectories are used instead and the substitution is reported.

Eligibility, fixed here. A lineage is included if it is tracked continuously for at least 20 generations with an identifiable division sequence. Lineages flagged by the tracking software as unreliable, and lineages whose channel is lost or overgrown, are excluded on the software's own flags rather than by our inspection.

Contingency tree, registered because the deposit's channel content is unverified by us. If the primary deposit contains a usable fluorescence channel with segmentable lineages, both arms run on it. If it lacks fluorescence, the timing arm — G0, H1, H2 — runs on the primary, and the expression arm — H3, H4, H5 — runs on the first reserve dataset carrying a reporter. Reserves, in order: the public mother-machine benchmark datasets used in that paper's own tools comparison, then any further public mother-machine deposit. Each reserve is usable only if it remains unopened by us at filing, and any reserve actually used is declared with its provenance before analysis.

Minimum viable sample, registered. A condition contributes to the confirmatory analysis only if it yields at least 30 eligible lineages. If no condition in the primary deposit reaches that count, the analysis moves to the reserve list under the same rule, and the shortfall is reported.

344-51.value: Fixed by the deposit; the counts are not known to us in advance. Two levels: lineages, and generations within lineage. Expected order of magnitude, from published descriptions of comparable experiments, is tens to hundreds of lineages per condition at twenty to seventy generations each; the actual counts, per condition, are reported once the deposit is processed. The disclosed pilot, which is not counted here, contained 279 lineages at approximately 69 generations across three temperatures.

344-53.value: No power analysis in the conventional sense: the sample is whatever the deposit contains. The registered minimum of 30 eligible lineages per condition exists because of H1's form rather than to reach a target power. H1 asserts a null, and a null is uninformative when imprecise — a small sample can return an intraclass correlation near zero simply for lack of information. The precision requirement attached to H1, that the upper bound of the 95 percent confidence interval fall below 0.15, is what makes the registered zero a claim rather than an absence of evidence, and it is the reason a minimum sample is specified at all. H3 to H5 concern within-lineage quantities computed over tens of generations per lineage and are correspondingly better constrained. Permutation inference is exact under the null at any sample size.

344-55.value:
Pilot work is complete and ended on a stated criterion: development stopped when the decomposition had been applied to the disclosed pilot dataset and the pipeline's constants were frozen and committed. No further development is planned.

Data collection begins after this registration is timestamped and proceeds in a single pass: the deposit is downloaded, processed under the rules above, and analyzed once. There are no interim analyses, no sequential accumulation, and no optional stopping. The reserve list is invoked only under the contingency conditions stated above, never because a result is unwelcome.

If the deposit cannot be obtained or cannot be processed within 90 days of registration, the analysis proceeds on the reserve list, and the failure and its cause are reported.

344-58.value: None. This is an observational secondary analysis. Growth conditions, including medium and temperature, were set by the original experimenters and are treated as strata: every registered quantity is computed within condition and the bars must be met in each.

344-62.value:
Raw, per lineage per generation: division events, from which interdivision time is derived; and fluorescence intensity, from which per-generation mean expression is derived.

Outcome quantities, computed per observable: intraclass correlation across lineages, per-lineage drift, per-lineage residue, and per-lineage lag-one autocorrelation of residuals.

Identifiers and strata: lineage identity, generation index, growth condition, and channel or position identifier where the deposit provides one.

Variables used for exclusion: number of continuously tracked generations per lineage, and the tracking software's own reliability flags.

Not available. Cell-internal state — damage accumulation, plasmid copy number, regulatory context — is not observable in these records. Lineage identity is quantified without attributing it to a specific molecular cause, and generation index serves as the ageing axis without implying a mechanism.

344-66.value:
Notation. For observable X and lineage l at generation g, x(l,g) is the measured value; N_l is the number of usable generations for lineage l. Both observables are analyzed on natural-log values.

1. Centering. C(l,g) = log x(l,g) minus the mean of log x over all lineages present at generation index g. All quantities below are computed on C, per condition.

2. Lineage identity. One-way random-effects intraclass correlation of C across lineages, estimated by the analysis-of-variance moment decomposition for unequal N_l. Inference by permutation: C shuffled across lineages within generation index, at least 500 shuffles. A 95 percent confidence interval is obtained by bootstrap resampling of lineages, 2000 resamples.

3. Drift, per lineage. Variance over g of the centered 5-generation rolling mean of C(l,·) about the mean of C(l,·). Summarized across lineages by median.

4. Residue, per lineage. Standard deviation over g of the successive differences of C(l,·), divided by the square root of two. Summarized across lineages by median.

5. Memory, per lineage. Lag-one autocorrelation of C(l,·) after removing that lineage's own mean. Summarized across lineages by median.

6. Units, fixed here. H5 compares variances: median drift against 0.5 times median residue squared, both in squared log units. H1 and H3 concern the intraclass correlation, which is dimensionless. H2 and H4 concern the autocorrelation, which is dimensionless.

344-71.value:
Every quantity is computed separately for each observable and each growth condition; nothing is pooled across observables, and results are reported per condition.

G0. The committed decomposition and test functions are run on the processed lineages. Failure to run, or any required amendment, is filed publicly before results are unblinded.

H1 and H3, lineage identity. One-way random-effects model C(l,g) = mu + a_l + e(l,g), with intraclass correlation var(a) / [var(a) + var(e)] from the analysis-of-variance moment estimator for unequal generation counts. Significance by permutation across lineages within generation index; confidence intervals by bootstrap resampling of lineages. H1 additionally requires the interval's upper bound to fall below 0.15, as registered.

H2 and H4, memory. Per-lineage lag-one autocorrelation of centered residuals; the median across lineages is compared with its registered threshold, with a bootstrap confidence interval and a sign test across lineages reported alongside.

H5, drift against residue. Per-lineage drift and residue; the ratio of medians compared with its registered bar, with a bootstrap confidence interval on the ratio.

Controls and assumption checks. The strongest control is internal: H3 is the within-dataset positive control for H1. A zero in the controlled observable is credible only because the carried observable, in the same cells and through the same pipeline, returns a clear positive with the same code. If both return zero, the honest reading is that the pipeline or the processing failed on this deposit, and that is what will be reported. The permutation null is the negative control for both. The pipeline's prior qualification on synthetic data with known components is uploaded with this registration. Drift depends on the 5-generation rolling window, so the analysis is repeated at windows 3 and 7 as a registered robustness check, with the 5-generation window remaining the registered definition. No test assumes normality; all inference is permutation- or bootstrap-based.

344-75.value: Both observables are analyzed on natural-log values, because interdivision times and fluorescence intensities are strictly positive and multiplicatively distributed; this matches the pilot and is not revisited. Values are then centered by generation index within condition, as specified under Indices. Growth condition is treated as a stratum rather than recoded. No other transformations are applied.

344-77.value:
H1: point estimate at most 0.05, permutation p above 0.10, and bootstrap interval upper bound below 0.15; all three required. Failing only the precision requirement is reported as underpowered, not as a pass and not as a failure of the claim. H3: point estimate at least 0.15, interval excluding 0.05, permutation p below 0.01. H2 and H4: median autocorrelation beyond its registered threshold in the registered direction, one-sided by construction since the direction is predicted. H5: threshold comparison against the registered ratio.

Multiplicity. Five confirmatory hypotheses, each against its own pre-set bar, each computed per condition, with the bars required in every condition. No alpha adjustment is applied and none is claimed; the full pass-and-fail pattern is reported per condition and per observable, and no hypothesis is substituted for another after the fact. The kill conditions in the Overview are evaluated exactly as written and take precedence over any favourable partial result.

344-79.value:
Included: all lineages tracked continuously for at least 20 generations in a condition yielding at least 30 such lineages.

Excluded, all criteria pre-specified: lineages shorter than 20 usable generations; lineages carrying the tracking software's own unreliability flags; lineages whose channel is lost, overgrown, or empty; and conditions yielding fewer than 30 eligible lineages, which are reported separately and descriptively rather than scored.

Outliers. No outlier removal. Unusually slow, fast, bright, or dim lineages are the between-lineage variation the analysis exists to quantify, and removing them would bias the very component under test. Exclusions rest on tracking reliability and series length only, never on the values themselves.

344-81.value: Missing values are not imputed. A generation with no usable measurement is treated as absent: per-lineage statistics use that lineage's available generations, and centering uses the lineages present at that generation index. Successive-difference and lag-one estimates skip gaps rather than bridging them, so residue and memory are computed only over adjacent observed generations. The number and position of missing generations is reported per lineage, and a lineage missing more than 20 percent of its generations within its tracked span is excluded and counted. Where an entire fluorescence channel is missing, the contingency tree on the Sampling page governs rather than any imputation.

344-83.value:
All of the following are secondary, declared exploratory, and unscored.

1. The ageing read: monotone trend of expression along the mother lineage, reported per condition with the fraction of lineages showing it. The pilot returned a median rank correlation of 0.32 with 92.5 percent of lineages positive at the highest temperature.
2. Two independence screens, disclosed because they bear on the assumption behind the permutation scheme. On the burned pilot, division events showed strong global co-timing consistent with shared conditions but no excess coincidence between physically adjacent lineages, and the expression channel showed no local excess either. Both screens are run on the registered deposit and reported; a local excess appearing there is reported as a design caveat on H1 to H5 rather than absorbed.
3. Rolling-window sensitivity for drift at windows 3, 5, and 7.
4. Temperature or condition comparison of every quantity, reported descriptively.
5. Comparison with the companion registrations in this slate, after all components have run

344-86.value:
This registration is the living-cell component of a slate applying one decomposition — stable identity, slow drift, generation-to-generation residue — to repeated measurements on individually identified units across substrates. Its companions cover repeated droplet freezing, solution crystallization, and collaborative work threads. Each stands alone with its own bars and kill conditions.

Why the mother machine. Most biological measurement pools cells and reports distributions, which discards the identity of the unit and makes the question here unaskable. Mother-machine experiments retain that identity across dozens of generations, and they supply two observables of the same cells that differ in exactly the relevant way: one is actively regulated by a known control mechanism, the other is not. That makes this the natural place to test whether control erases identity in the variable it regulates.

What is at stake. If the timing zero fails to reproduce in another laboratory's data, the erasure claim is wrong and we will report it as wrong. If both observables return zero, the honest conclusion is a processing or pipeline failure on this deposit rather than a finding, and that is registered in advance. If the contrast holds, the practical consequence is a cheap diagnostic — the sign of one-generation memory — for deciding whether a measured quantity in a lineage experiment is under control or carried, which is a distinction currently drawn from mechanism rather than from data.

Code and data availability. The committed decomposition and test script, the two independence-screen scripts, and the synthetic-qualification script with its frozen expectations are uploaded with this registration. On completion, per-lineage rows — decomposition components, memory, condition, and generation counts — will be deposited in the associated project as rows rather than summaries, so that any reader can recompute every reported quantity.

Declarations. No funding. No competing interests. The work is conducted without institutional affiliation; pre-registration is used here as the mechanism that makes the claims checkable independently of their author, with bars, kill conditions, and disclosures fixed in advance and outcomes reported regardless of direction.

registration_responses.344-62:
Raw, per lineage per generation: division events, from which interdivision time is derived; and fluorescence intensity, from which per-generation mean expression is derived.

Outcome quantities, computed per observable: intraclass correlation across lineages, per-lineage drift, per-lineage residue, and per-lineage lag-one autocorrelation of residuals.

Identifiers and strata: lineage identity, generation index, growth condition, and channel or position identifier where the deposit provides one.

Variables used for exclusion: number of continuously tracked generations per lineage, and the tracking software's own reliability flags.

Not available. Cell-internal state — damage accumulation, plasmid copy number, regulatory context — is not observable in these records. Lineage identity is quantified without attributing it to a specific molecular cause, and generation index serves as the ageing axis without implying a mechanism.
registration_responses.344-66:
Notation. For observable X and lineage l at generation g, x(l,g) is the measured value; N_l is the number of usable generations for lineage l. Both observables are analyzed on natural-log values.

1. Centering. C(l,g) = log x(l,g) minus the mean of log x over all lineages present at generation index g. All quantities below are computed on C, per condition.

2. Lineage identity. One-way random-effects intraclass correlation of C across lineages, estimated by the analysis-of-variance moment decomposition for unequal N_l. Inference by permutation: C shuffled across lineages within generation index, at least 500 shuffles. A 95 percent confidence interval is obtained by bootstrap resampling of lineages, 2000 resamples.

3. Drift, per lineage. Variance over g of the centered 5-generation rolling mean of C(l,·) about the mean of C(l,·). Summarized across lineages by median.

4. Residue, per lineage. Standard deviation over g of the successive differences of C(l,·), divided by the square root of two. Summarized across lineages by median.

5. Memory, per lineage. Lag-one autocorrelation of C(l,·) after removing that lineage's own mean. Summarized across lineages by median.

6. Units, fixed here. H5 compares variances: median drift against 0.5 times median residue squared, both in squared log units. H1 and H3 concern the intraclass correlation, which is dimensionless. H2 and H4 concern the autocorrelation, which is dimensionless.
registration_responses.344-71:
Every quantity is computed separately for each observable and each growth condition; nothing is pooled across observables, and results are reported per condition.

G0. The committed decomposition and test functions are run on the processed lineages. Failure to run, or any required amendment, is filed publicly before results are unblinded.

H1 and H3, lineage identity. One-way random-effects model C(l,g) = mu + a_l + e(l,g), with intraclass correlation var(a) / [var(a) + var(e)] from the analysis-of-variance moment estimator for unequal generation counts. Significance by permutation across lineages within generation index; confidence intervals by bootstrap resampling of lineages. H1 additionally requires the interval's upper bound to fall below 0.15, as registered.

H2 and H4, memory. Per-lineage lag-one autocorrelation of centered residuals; the median across lineages is compared with its registered threshold, with a bootstrap confidence interval and a sign test across lineages reported alongside.

H5, drift against residue. Per-lineage drift and residue; the ratio of medians compared with its registered bar, with a bootstrap confidence interval on the ratio.

Controls and assumption checks. The strongest control is internal: H3 is the within-dataset positive control for H1. A zero in the controlled observable is credible only because the carried observable, in the same cells and through the same pipeline, returns a clear positive with the same code. If both return zero, the honest reading is that the pipeline or the processing failed on this deposit, and that is what will be reported. The permutation null is the negative control for both. The pipeline's prior qualification on synthetic data with known components is uploaded with this registration. Drift depends on the 5-generation rolling window, so the analysis is repeated at windows 3 and 7 as a registered robustness check, with the 5-generation window remaining the registered definition. No test assumes normality; all inference is permutation- or bootstrap-based.
registration_responses.344-75: Both observables are analyzed on natural-log values, because interdivision times and fluorescence intensities are strictly positive and multiplicatively distributed; this matches the pilot and is not revisited. Values are then centered by generation index within condition, as specified under Indices. Growth condition is treated as a stratum rather than recoded. No other transformations are applied.
registration_responses.344-77:
H1: point estimate at most 0.05, permutation p above 0.10, and bootstrap interval upper bound below 0.15; all three required. Failing only the precision requirement is reported as underpowered, not as a pass and not as a failure of the claim. H3: point estimate at least 0.15, interval excluding 0.05, permutation p below 0.01. H2 and H4: median autocorrelation beyond its registered threshold in the registered direction, one-sided by construction since the direction is predicted. H5: threshold comparison against the registered ratio.

Multiplicity. Five confirmatory hypotheses, each against its own pre-set bar, each computed per condition, with the bars required in every condition. No alpha adjustment is applied and none is claimed; the full pass-and-fail pattern is reported per condition and per observable, and no hypothesis is substituted for another after the fact. The kill conditions in the Overview are evaluated exactly as written and take precedence over any favourable partial result.
registration_responses.344-79:
Included: all lineages tracked continuously for at least 20 generations in a condition yielding at least 30 such lineages.

Excluded, all criteria pre-specified: lineages shorter than 20 usable generations; lineages carrying the tracking software's own unreliability flags; lineages whose channel is lost, overgrown, or empty; and conditions yielding fewer than 30 eligible lineages, which are reported separately and descriptively rather than scored.

Outliers. No outlier removal. Unusually slow, fast, bright, or dim lineages are the between-lineage variation the analysis exists to quantify, and removing them would bias the very component under test. Exclusions rest on tracking reliability and series length only, never on the values themselves.
registration_responses.344-81: Missing values are not imputed. A generation with no usable measurement is treated as absent: per-lineage statistics use that lineage's available generations, and centering uses the lineages present at that generation index. Successive-difference and lag-one estimates skip gaps rather than bridging them, so residue and memory are computed only over adjacent observed generations. The number and position of missing generations is reported per lineage, and a lineage missing more than 20 percent of its generations within its tracked span is excluded and counted. Where an entire fluorescence channel is missing, the contingency tree on the Sampling page governs rather than any imputation.
registration_responses.344-83:
All of the following are secondary, declared exploratory, and unscored.

1. The ageing read: monotone trend of expression along the mother lineage, reported per condition with the fraction of lineages showing it. The pilot returned a median rank correlation of 0.32 with 92.5 percent of lineages positive at the highest temperature.
2. Two independence screens, disclosed because they bear on the assumption behind the permutation scheme. On the burned pilot, division events showed strong global co-timing consistent with shared conditions but no excess coincidence between physically adjacent lineages, and the expression channel showed no local excess either. Both screens are run on the registered deposit and reported; a local excess appearing there is reported as a design caveat on H1 to H5 rather than absorbed.
3. Rolling-window sensitivity for drift at windows 3, 5, and 7.
4. Temperature or condition comparison of every quantity, reported descriptively.
5. Comparison with the companion registrations in this slate, after all components have run
registration_responses.344-86:
This registration is the living-cell component of a slate applying one decomposition — stable identity, slow drift, generation-to-generation residue — to repeated measurements on individually identified units across substrates. Its companions cover repeated droplet freezing, solution crystallization, and collaborative work threads. Each stands alone with its own bars and kill conditions.

Why the mother machine. Most biological measurement pools cells and reports distributions, which discards the identity of the unit and makes the question here unaskable. Mother-machine experiments retain that identity across dozens of generations, and they supply two observables of the same cells that differ in exactly the relevant way: one is actively regulated by a known control mechanism, the other is not. That makes this the natural place to test whether control erases identity in the variable it regulates.

What is at stake. If the timing zero fails to reproduce in another laboratory's data, the erasure claim is wrong and we will report it as wrong. If both observables return zero, the honest conclusion is a processing or pipeline failure on this deposit rather than a finding, and that is registered in advance. If the contrast holds, the practical consequence is a cheap diagnostic — the sign of one-generation memory — for deciding whether a measured quantity in a lineage experiment is under control or carried, which is a distinction currently drawn from mechanism rather than from data.

Code and data availability. The committed decomposition and test script, the two independence-screen scripts, and the synthetic-qualification script with its frozen expectations are uploaded with this registration. On completion, per-lineage rows — decomposition components, memory, condition, and generation counts — will be deposited in the associated project as rows rather than summaries, so that any reader can recompute every reported quantity.

Declarations. No funding. No competing interests. The work is conducted without institutional affiliation; pre-registration is used here as the mechanism that makes the claims checkable independently of their author, with bars, kill conditions, and disclosures fixed in advance and outcomes reported regardless of direction.

attributes.title: FRONT 3.1: A Homeostatic Regulation Architecture and Digital Somatic Body
attributes.description: artificial intelligence, homeostatic regulation, interoceptive architecture, language models, cognitive base
tags: artificial intelligence homeostatic regulation interoceptive architecture language models cognitive base

summary.value: This registration documents the original conceptual proposal of FRONT 3.1 (Front Regulatory Organism for Needs and Valence Theory), an architectural framework establishing a Digital Somatic Body as a necessary foundation for artificial cognitive systems. The central thesis is that cognition without a persistent affective-interoceptive base is processing — not cognition. The proposal includes a continuous six-dimensional interoceptive state vector with stochastic homeostatic update dynamics, a three-stage pre-cognitive causality flow, somatically marked affective memory with valence-driven retrieval, an autobiographical self-model, and six falsifiable predictions with defined operational metrics. The central empirical prediction — Emergent Uniqueness (P5) — states that agents sharing identical architecture and initial training but exposed to distinct histories will diverge systematically in decision distributions, formalizable via KL Divergence. This registration establishes priority of authorship for Anderson Cabral, independent researcher, São Paulo, Brazil, August 2026.
